title: Reusable Terraform module for VPC access role patterns with least-privilege defaults
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a general-purpose Terraform module that codifies VPC-facing role and permission patterns for Redwood Private deployments. The module should produce minimal, auditable IAM role definitions (assume-role principals, permission boundaries, scoped managed policies) and helper resources for cross-account trust and service-linked roles. It must be opinionated but configurable, with sane least-privilege defaults and explicit override hooks for customers who need extra entitlements.

Scope:
- Terraform 1.5+ HCL module suitable for use inside the priv-deploy reference stack.
- Support for both AWS IAM roles and an abstracted config to later add GCP service accounts.
- Outputs: role ARNs, policy ARNs, recommended policy diffs for upgrades.
- Migration tooling: import mapping + a one-shot plan to align existing stacks to the module.
- Automated policy validation and periodic health checks (drift detection + permissions smoke tests).

Non-goals: Not building the entire RBAC system or UI. Not implementing customer-facing RBAC rules in Console in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes on internal Terraform registry (artifact path) and can be consumed by priv-deploy reference stack with <= 3 input params for default use
Default role definitions follow principle of least privilege: no wildcard actions on write resources, scoped ARNs, explicit allow for required service actions
Module produces a migration script (terraform import map + sample tfstate commands) and a documented upgrade checklist
CI runs policy linter (tfsec/custom rules) and a terratest suite that asserts: AssumeRole works, permission boundary enforced, and common admin actions are denied
A scheduled health-check job is added that validates final effective policies against expected role capabilities and alerts on drift
implementation_plan:
1) Design phase (2 days): finalize input schema and policy templates; collaborate with Security on permission boundary shape. 2) Build (3 days): implement HCL module, minimal tests, helper scripts for import. 3) Integrate (2 days): consume module in priv-deploy reference stack and run migration on staging. 4) Validation (2 days): run CI/terratest and security review. 5) Rollout (1 day): publish module, update docs and sample templates.

Key implementation decisions: use managed policy documents generated by locals + templatefile to avoid monolithic JSON; enforce permission_boundary via role config; provide 'extra_statements' input as list(string) to avoid ad-hoc inline patches; expose a 'trust_principals' map for cross-account mappings.

Artifacts: Confluence sketch https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-31472-role-patterns, RFC doc link, and initial draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/482.
testing_plan:
- Unit: terraform validate + fmt in CI.
- Lint: tfsec + custom policy checks to block broad actions.
- Integration: terratest that: creates temp stack, attempts allowed operations (e.g., put-object to S3 bucket if role scoped), attempts denied operations (e.g., iam:CreateUser) and asserts failure.
- Migration dry-run on staging environment using the import map and audit of resulting plan.
- Post-merge: schedule nightly drift detection job for two weeks to catch any unexpected policy changes.
health_checks: Policy drift detector: scheduled Lambda that compares current role policy document to module-generated canonical policy and opens an alert if >10% statement divergence
Smoke test runner: ephemeral credentials assume-role + execute a set of queries (S3 read/write, CloudWatch logs append) based on role template; failures create incident ticket
CI gate: any PR that changes module must run terratest and policy-lint and require security sign-off
migration_notes:
- Provide terraform-import mapping: map legacy role names to module-managed resources and include example 'terraform state mv' commands.
- Create a small wrapper module (compat-mode) that mirrors legacy attribute names to new inputs for smoother upgrade.
- For customers with manual custom policies, include a diff tool that shows removed privileges and suggested mitigations.
- Rollout strategy: stage -> canary (one customer stack) -> full. Acquire customer opt-in for canary where possible.

notes_for_oncall: If drift detector alerts, first step is to run the module's canonical policy generator against the target stack and compare. If divergence is caused by an emergency hotfix, record the exception and create follow-up ENG ticket to incorporate the fix into the module. Critical incidents: revoke temporary credentials and rotate any affected keys immediately.
